claim: On 201 Japanese insight riddles, reasoning models often produce the correct candidate in their thought log but do not endorse it as the final answer (verification failure).
quote: models generate a correct intermediate candidate but fail to endorse it as their final answer
authors: Mizumoto, Nguyen, Han, Li, Nakawake, Nguyen
title: The Metacognitive Bottleneck: Japanese Riddles Reveal Fundamental Limits of Machine Insight and Self-Evaluation in Reasoning AI
transfer: After a solve attempt, keep every intermediate candidate in a list and run a separate selector call over all candidates instead of trusting the last one.

claim: On the same riddles, non-reasoning models reach 7.6% accuracy and reasoning models 17.6%, against a human mean of 52.9%; verification failures are 5% to 39% of wrong answers for models with usable logs.
quote: non-reasoning models achieve 7.6% accuracy and reasoning-oriented models reach 17.6%
title: The Metacognitive Bottleneck (NazoNazo benchmark)
transfer: Insight-style items are a hard test set for representation-change steps; track candidates-generated versus candidate-chosen as a metric.

claim: Chain-of-thought can reduce model accuracy on tasks where verbal deliberation also hurts humans; 3 of 6 tested tasks showed significant drops, up to 36.3 points for o1-preview vs GPT-4o.
authors: Liu, Geng, Wu, Sucholutsky, Lombrozo, Griffiths
title: Mind Your Step (by Step): Chain-of-Thought can Reduce Performance on Tasks where Thinking Makes Humans Worse
transfer: Router rule: if the task type is one where human deliberation hurts (pattern or implicit learning, exceptions), skip the slow step. Matches our puzzle result. No verbatim span captured; abstract was summarized by the fetch tool.

claim: A secondary summary reports an artificial-grammar style task where o1-preview scored about 58.6% and GPT-4o about 95%, so more deliberation lost on implicit pattern tasks.
title: Mind Your Step (by Step) summary
transfer: Add an implicit-pattern class to the router that uses the plain first answer. Numbers come from a secondary summary, not the paper.

claim: Best reasoning agent (o3-mini high with code execution) creates valid counterexamples for under 9% of incorrect solutions on REFUTE, though it could solve up to 48% of the same problems from scratch.
authors: Sinha, Goel, Kumaraguru, Geiping, Bethge, Prabhu
title: Can Language Models Falsify? Evaluating Algorithmic Reasoning with Counterexample Creation
transfer: Johnson-Laird counterexample search is weak in models. Do not rely on a free-text 'find a counterexample' call; ground it in code that runs the rule on new inputs.

claim: PaLM 2 models on syllogisms: larger models are more logical than smaller ones and than humans, yet still make systematic errors that mirror human bias, such as sensitivity to irrelevant term order.
authors: Eisape, Tessler, Dasgupta, Sha, van Steenkiste, Linzen
title: A Systematic Comparison of Syllogistic Reasoning in Humans and Language Models
transfer: Reorder premises or terms and re-ask: disagreement flags a bias-driven answer. Cheap permutation check.

claim: MedEinst: 5,383 paired clinical cases over 49 diseases and 17 LLMs; each trap case alters evidence so the common diagnosis is wrong; the Bias Trap Rate measures misdiagnosing the trap after getting the control right.
quote: relying on statistical shortcuts rather than patient-specific evidence
title: MedEinst: Benchmarking the Einstellung Effect in Medical LLMs through Counterfactual Differential Diagnosis
transfer: Einstellung test for the agent: pair each task with a variant where the familiar answer is wrong, and measure the trap rate with and without a diversity step. The 'stronger models more biased' claim came from a search summary, not verified in the fetched abstract.

claim: Tree of Thoughts treats reasoning as search over thoughts with generation, state evaluation and search steps; on Game of 24 (100 hard games) GPT-4 chain-of-thought solved about 4% and ToT about 74%.
title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
transfer: Problem-space search is a real gain on tasks with a checkable intermediate state (arithmetic, planning). Use only where a state evaluator exists. Numbers from search snippets of the NeurIPS poster page.

claim: GPT-4 average success on autonomous plan generation across IPC-like domains was about 12%; external verifiers that back-prompt the LLM (LLM-Modulo) are proposed as the fix.
title: On the Planning Abilities of Large Language Models: A Critical Investigation
transfer: Generate in the model, verify outside it with a program. Matches our executor design.

claim: o1 models improve planning over plain LLMs at steep inference cost and without guarantees; pairing them with external verifiers (LRM-Modulo) guarantees output correctness and improves performance further.
title: LLMs Still Can't Plan; Can LRMs? A Preliminary Evaluation of OpenAI's o1 on PlanBench
transfer: Keep a verifier loop even with strong reasoning models; do not assume thinking tokens replace checking.

claim: Apple's Illusion of Thinking reports three regimes on controllable puzzles: plain LLMs match or beat reasoning variants at low complexity, reasoning helps at medium, both collapse at high.
authors: Shojaee, Mirzadeh, Bengio, Farajtabar et al.
title: The Illusion of Thinking
transfer: Fits our data: slow steps lose on easy items. Route by difficulty. Secondary source only; disk counts differ across summaries.

claim: A rebuttal argues the Hanoi collapse reflects output token limits and that River Crossing had impossible instances scored as failures; asking for a generating function gave high accuracy.
title: The Illusion of the Illusion of Thinking
transfer: Ask the model for a program that solves the class, not a long move list: representation change that avoids the budget wall. Author names from memory, not checked.

claim: Reasoning models can disregard a correct solution even when it is given, and keep generating extra steps that lead to wrong conclusions (AIME2024, 3 models).
quote: disregard correct solutions even when explicitly provided
title: Large Reasoning Models are not thinking straight: on the unreliability of thinking trajectories
transfer: Stop rule: once a candidate passes an external check, end the thinking loop. Do not let the model keep deliberating.

claim: Language models, like people, answer logic tasks (NLI, syllogism validity, Wason selection) more accurately when semantic content supports the logical inference (content effects).
quote: answer more accurately when the semantic content of a task supports the logical inferences
title: Language models, like humans, show content effects on reasoning tasks
transfer: Rewrite a problem with abstract or neutral content (representation change) and compare answers; a flip shows a belief-driven answer.

claim: GPT-3 era models showed human-like intuitive errors on cognitive reflection tests and semantic illusions; ChatGPT models mostly avoided them and stayed accurate even when chain-of-thought was blocked.
quote: remain accurate when prevented from doing so
title: Human-like intuitive behavior and reasoning biases emerged in large language models but disappeared in ChatGPT
n: CRT and semantic illusion item sets
transfer: Do not assume trap questions need slow steps for modern models. Test it. Contamination of CRT items is a raised concern (PsyPost coverage).

claim: Two-response studies find correct logical answers often appear in the first, immediate response under time pressure and load, so deliberation is not always what fixes a biased first answer.
quote: frequently observe correct, logical responses as the first, immediate response
title: The smart System 1: evidence for the intuitive nature of correct responding on the bat-and-ball problem / Fast logic? time course assumption of dual process theory
venue: Thinking and Reasoning (title and venue not confirmed)
transfer: Supports a trust-first-answer default: the first sample is often right, so use slow steps only when a conflict signal appears. Exact title unconfirmed.

claim: In a later two-response study, in more than half of the cases with a correct final response, the initial response was already correct.
quote: in more than half of the cases when the response was correct in the final response stage, it was already correct at the initial response stage
title: Logical intuition is not really about logic
venue: Journal of Experimental Psychology: General (venue from memory; search listed gwern copy 2022-ghasemi.pdf)
transfer: Measure how often our scaffold changes a right first answer to wrong; this is the human base rate to compare against. Authors and title from memory.

claim: De Neys's revised dual-process view says both heuristic and logical intuitions are generated automatically, and deliberation mainly matters when they conflict at similar strength.
title: Advancing theorizing about fast-and-slow thinking
venue: Behavioral and Brain Sciences (commentary volume; critiques by Sherman and Klein, Sirota, Stupple and Ball)
transfer: Conflict detector: draft two or more fast answers, and spend slow effort only if they differ in substance. Title from memory; summary came from search results.

claim: Self-consistency across many samples can be well calibrated when the model is mostly right, but amplifies confidence in errors when the model is systematically wrong (stable hallucination); the analysis assumes i.i.d. samples.
title: Black-Box Reliability Certification for AI Agents via Self-Consistency Sampling and Conformal Calibration
transfer: Agreement is a signal only when an external check exists; otherwise it can confirm a shared error. Matches our correlated-samples finding.

claim: A grading study found asking the model for its own confidence gave better calibration than self-consistency (ECE 0.166 vs 0.229) at about one fifth the inference cost.
title: When Can We Trust LLM Graders? Calibrating Confidence for Automated Assessment
transfer: Challenges the earlier brief's rule to avoid stated confidence. Test both signals on our items before choosing.

claim: Klahr and Dunbar's dual-space model has been extended to a 4-space model (Schunn and Klahr 1995); the search found no paper that applies dual-space search to LLM agents by name, and LLM-AutoSciLab (2026) reports hypothesis-guided experiment selection is 2-5x more sample efficient than baselines.
title: LLM-AutoSciLab: Closed-Loop Scientific Discovery via Active Experimentation with LLMs
transfer: Keep two logs, a hypothesis list and an experiment list, and choose the next experiment to split the hypotheses. Efficiency claim unverified.

claim: Aha experience is not a clean marker of restructuring: in one study 56.1% of correct insight solutions came with Aha; chess players solved the mutilated checkerboard better yet reported less Aha.
title: Aha experience and insight solving studies (several 2019 to 2026 papers)
venue: journals listed in search; not opened
transfer: Do not trigger on the model saying it had an insight. Trigger on measurable change: new representation plus a check that passes.
